claims.text: Rapid cooling at 10^5–10^6 K/s produces an almost fully amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy.
The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy undergoes extensive primary crystallization during slower cooling.
The rapidly cooled amorphous alloy is prone to crystallization during uncontrolled reheating.
A well-timed reheating pulse immediately after melt-spinning will induce a glass-to-glass transition in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The proposed pulse is a short-duration sub-Tg anneal below the onset of crystallization.
The effective reheating window is approximately 900–1200 K.
The crystallization onset of the target alloy is around 1200 K.
An initial cooling rate exceeding 10^5 K/s is required for the intervention to be effective.
Beneficial atomic rearrangement requires reheating well above the glass-transition temperature.
Reheating will enhance chemical short-range order and induce local atomic rearrangements in the amorphous matrix.
The enhanced ordering and rearrangements will lock in the disordered state.
The pulse provides enough atomic mobility for stress relaxation.
A heating-induced transition between distinct amorphous states can occur in a high-entropy metallic glass.
The glass-to-glass transition will impede nucleation and growth of primary crystalline phases in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The pulse-treated alloy will retain a larger amorphous fraction than rapidly cooled-only or slowly cooled samples.
The pulse-treated alloy will exhibit a higher crystallization onset temperature during subsequent thermal analysis.
A glass-to-glass transition can significantly improve the thermal stability, modulus, and hardness of a metallic glass.
The precise pulse temperature and duration require experimental optimization.
The detailed atomic-scale dynamics of the proposed glass-to-glass transition remain incompletely characterized.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant crystallization-onset delay and greater amorphous retention, or observation of increased crystallization, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is repeatedly described as sub-Tg, but the boundary states that reheating must be well above the glass-transition temperature.
The proposed window extends to 1200 K while crystallization onset is itself stated to be around 1200 K, conflicting with the requirement that the pulse remain carefully below crystallization onset.
